News

All news
  • Research & Expertise

    ‘Putting Forward Theories Is the Last Skill at Which We Outperform Machines’

    Louis Vervoort, Associate Professor at the HSE Tikhonov Moscow Institute of Electronics and Mathematics (HSE MIEM) and specialist in the philosophy of science and artificial intelligence, spoke to the HSE News Service about what physics and philosophy have in common, why quantum mechanics is incompatible with the theory of relativity, what it means to be a researcher in the age of AI, and why the ability to develop new theories may become humanity’s greatest advantage over machines.

  • Community

    'Meeting Students from Different Countries Helped Me Understand How People Approach Education and Learning in Different Contexts’

    Hasnain is a student of the Master’s in Science of Learning and Assessment (SOLA) programme at the HSE University Institute of Education from Baffa, Pakistan. Now in his second year of studies, he has had time to experience much of what HSE University and Moscow have to offer international students. Read on to learn about Hasnain’s experiences of the diversity of perspectives at HSE, representing Pakistani culture, and Moscow’s unique atmosphere of contrasts.
     

  • Education

    HSE University Students Develop Socially Significant Project in Digital Healthcare

    In October 2026, Sechenov University hosted MedITron, a medical innovation hackathon. Over three days, participants were challenged to develop a solution to one of the case studies prepared by leading MedTech organisations. Among the winners was Team Med404, which included two HSE students.

  • Education

    HSE Experts Instruct Statisticians for Upcoming National Survey of Time Budgets in Turkmenistan

    At the end of October, experts of the HSE Human Capital Multidisciplinary Research Centre of the Institute for Social Policy conducted comprehensive training for specialists of the State Committee of Turkmenistan on Statistics. The event, organised within the framework of the UNFPA CISPop programme, the HSE project ‘Development of Interdisciplinary Human Potential Research’ (HSE-MS-2026-105), as well as with the support of UNDP, was a key step in the preparations for the first national sample survey on the use of daily time by the population in the country's history.

  • Research & Expertise

    HSE Scientists Present Tensor Methods Research at International Conference in China

    Researchers from the AI and Digital Science Institute at the HSE Faculty of Computer Science took part in the 3rd Conference–School on Tensor Methods in Mathematics and Artificial Intelligence Computing. The event was held in Shenzhen, China, in late October 2026. One of the institute's research projects received the Best Poster Award, placing among the conference's five best posters.

  • Research & Expertise

    Physicists Train AI to Optimise Particle Beams in Accelerators

    Researchers from the HSE AI and Digital Science Institute and the Budker Institute of Nuclear Physics have developed RLABC (Reinforcement Learning for Accelerator Beamline Control), a framework that uses reinforcement learning to identify optimal settings for a particle accelerator. In a computer simulation, RLABC optimised the accelerator's parameters to achieve a particle transmission rate of 70%. 

  • Society

    HSE University and GES-2 Open Call for Papers for Fourth ‘Researching Deaf Community’ Conference

    The International Laboratory for Social Integration Research at HSE University and the GES-2 House of Culture are jointly organising the Fourth Interdisciplinary Conference ‘Researching the Deaf Community,’ which will focus on the theme ‘Everyone Has Their Own Voice.’ Scheduled for June 2027, the conference will explore the diversity of voices within the Deaf community and the right to be heard in one's own language.

  • Education

    Moscow Hosts Closing Ceremony of the First-Ever International Space Games

    Teams of young people and students from eight countries—China, India, Kazakhstan, Kyrgyzstan, Mexico, Pakistan, Uzbekistan, and Russia—successfully completed the main mission of the International Space Games (ISG): ensuring the sustainable functioning of an autonomous settlement on another planet. The Games’ unique format, which dispenses with traditional competition aimed at securing victory for a single country, has proved its effectiveness. HSE University is the project operator.

  • Research & Expertise

    New Opportunities for Nature-Based Climate Projects: Technologies, Digital Tools, and Development Prospects

    Nature-based climate projects have significant potential, but its realisation requires more than promising technologies: a scientific foundation, clear methodologies, digital tools, and sustained demand for carbon credits. How can these elements turn individual initiatives into scalable solutions? This was the question discussed by participants at a conference organised by the HSE Сentre of Digital Technologies for Nature-Based Solutions of the Carbon Measurement Supersites Programme.

Student Voices

HSE has broadened my academic perspective and deepened my interest in research. It has helped me become more confident in my skills, more open to interdisciplinary work, and more determined to contribute meaningfully to the field of language education and applied linguistics.

Mujing Raissa Mij (the Democratic Republic of the Congo), Master’s Programme in Linguistic Theory and Language Description

I liked the approach that always challenged you to learn more. Every course encouraged us to do some research on our own. My research skills helped me a lot in my career.

Luis Santaella (Mexico), Bachelor’s Programme 'Political Science and World Politics'

HSE has a lively and international academic atmosphere that encourages critical thinking and interdisciplinary learning. I like how classes are structured to promote discussion rather than just passive learning. There’s a strong emphasis on research, so students are encouraged to explore their own interests and develop analytical skills.

Adila Ulfia Maula Tontowi (Indonesia), Bachelor’s Programme in Foreign Languages and Intercultural Communication

The HSE alumni network has been incredibly supportive. It connects students and professionals from around the world who share similar experiences. I’ve met many alumni who have offered advice, mentorship, and even research collaborations, both in academia and industry.

Warda Tariq (Pakistan), Master’s Programme in Data Science

I chose HSE University because of its academic excellence and international recognition. The university offers a strong Russian language programme and many opportunities for personal and professional growth.

Nguyen Xuan Thanh (Vietnam), HSE Preparatory Year

One of the things I find truly unique about the academic process at HSE is the composition of the teaching staff: it is a balanced mix of theorists and practicing professionals.

Dilmurod Kholmatov (Uzbekistan), Master’s Programme in Law of International Trade and Dispute Resolution

HSE University offers a globally competitive curriculum and has strong collaborations with international institutions. The research opportunities and the chance to work on real-world projects were key factors that motivated me to choose my programme at HSE.

Kartik Joshi (India), Master's Programme in Data Science
